summary: The harness is in good mechanical shape — Go build/vet/test (incl. -race), 22 hook tests, 79 skill tests and docs_check all pass, there is no command injection in Go or Python, and no OS/cache junk is tracked. The issues are in what the gates actually guarantee rather than in whether they run: tdd-guard accepts any failing-then-passing command as red→green, build-guard fails open without jq and is bypassable in a dozen ordinary ways while also blocking benign commands, the installers copy-or-symlink inconsistently and can shadow or delete user files, and the agents reference four skills that do not exist in the single-source tree. Parity across harnesses is strong in prose but weak in enforcement: Codex has no hooks and Antigravity has no Stop gate. Documentation (README, ADRs, CHANGELOG) has drifted from the code in several specific places.

recommendations.title: Make tdd-guard prove red→green on the same command
recommendations.detail: verify currently accepts any argv that exits 0 after any argv that exited non-zero (`--red-command false` / `--green-command true` passes). Store the red ArgvDigest at seal time and require verify's green argv to match it (or at least the same test runner), and re-check sealed-test digests after the green run. If the argv is meant to be fixed by the build skill rather than the agent, say so explicitly in the builder agent and SKILL.md.

recommendations.title: Decide what build-guard is, then make it that
recommendations.detail: Its header says 'deliberately narrow'; README says it 'blocks critical violations'. If it is a boundary: fail closed (exit 2 with a reason) when jq or tdd-guard is missing, cover bare `git push`, `git branch -f main`, `git update-ref`, `gh pr merge`, quoted `--target-dir "/tmp/x"` and `--target-dir /tmp`, and stop matching inside commit messages and `main-*` branch names. If it is advisory: change the README wording and drop the 'blocking' claim. Either way add the probe cases to test_hooks.sh.

recommendations.title: Make install/uninstall symlink-only, ownership-checked, and hermetic in tests
recommendations.detail: project-bootstrap.sh --install copies hooks (install -m755) while bootstrap-tools.sh symlinks them, so the README's 'edit here, takes effect immediately' claim breaks after the former runs — and test_hooks.sh runs it, clobbering ~/.local/bin on every test and CI run. Use ln -sfn everywhere; before ln or rm, check the target is absent or a symlink into $ROOT (readlink) and refuse otherwise; point test_hooks.sh at a temp BIN/HOME.

recommendations.title: Remove or add the four skills the agents reference but the tree lacks
recommendations.detail: read-the-damn-docs and find-docs (all research agents, README), grill-with-docs (all docs agents, README) do not exist anywhere. full-output-enforcement exists only in the gitignored .agents/skills/, so Codex/Antigravity and any fresh clone cannot resolve it. Either move them under skills/ or delete the references; add a test that every skill named in agents/**/*.md exists under skills/.

recommendations.title: Close the enforcement gap on Codex and Antigravity
recommendations.detail: Only the Claude builder wires PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop/SubagentStop. Antigravity has no Stop hook, so `build-hooks agy Stop` (the TDD verify gate) never runs; Codex wires no hooks at all, so build-guard and tdd-guard do not apply there. Codex/agy builders are also told to spawn a code-reviewer without declaring a tool for it, and agy runs the builder on `model: flash`. Either wire the hooks (or document the harness limitation in README) and align model tiers.

recommendations.title: Fix the recursive-glob false negative in build wave overlap detection
recommendations.detail: globs_overlap uses PurePath.match, which is right-anchored and does not treat `**` recursively on 3.13, so `src/**` vs `src/a/b/c.py` reports no overlap and both issues land in the same wave. Use PurePath.full_match (3.13+) or an fnmatch-based expansion, exclude wave 0 (ungrouped) from the check, and add the deep-path case to test_build.py.

recommendations.title: Harden the planner/review renderers and reconciler round-trip
recommendations.detail: validate_plan validates the stripped id but keeps the raw one, so whitespace-padded planId/issue keys produce markers the reconciler never matches and every run re-creates all issues — normalise or reject. Both render scripts substitute {{TOKENS}} sequentially, so user text containing a later token name pulls that section's markup in; switch to a single-pass re.sub (the new research renderer already does this).

recommendations.title: Make CI discover every skill suite and add the lint gates the hooks rely on
recommendations.detail: review-fix-loop's 12 tests are tracked but not run, and the docs test that guards ci.yml only knows the five older skills. Loop over skills/*/tests in ci.yml, pin Python with actions/setup-python, and add `ruff check skills/` (44 style findings today) and `shellcheck scripts/**` steps so the build-lint hook's assumptions are exercised somewhere.

recommendations.title: Make install-harness.sh run on stock macOS
recommendations.detail: `find -printf` is GNU-only and `mapfile` needs bash 4+, so the documented entry point aborts with 'no skills found' on a default macOS. Use a portable loop over skills/*/ and drop mapfile. Also add `set -e` (or explicit checks) so a failed step does not still print 'done.'

recommendations.title: Guard GitHub reconciliation against mid-build parameter drift
recommendations.detail: Planner re-reconcile reopens issues builders closed; reconcile_findings closes issues that merely fell below a stricter --min-severity; loop_state stores --min-severity but never uses it, so a nit-only review never converges. Skip closed/status:done issues on planner reconcile, compare recorded severity before closing, and wire (or remove) the loop's --min-severity.

recommendations.title: Bring README, ADRs and CHANGELOG back in line with the code
recommendations.detail: ADR-0001 is still 'Accepted' though superseded in practice; ADR-0002 says Antigravity files are copied (they are symlinked) and omits the dist/ step for Codex; CHANGELOG lacks the last two feature commits; README overstates streaming-digest coverage, '--uninstall reverses it', and hook parity, and names the binary tdd-guard while its usage text says anvil-guard (and --help exits 1). Document the `status:done` label waves.py honours.

recommendations.title: Trim dead code and fix the misleading validator comment
recommendations.detail: guard.filesMatchingGlob is unreachable; ten exported controlplane functions (Seal*/Validate*/Decode*) have no callers or tests — either an external consumer exists (document it) or trim/cover them. ValidIdentifier's comment claims to exclude path traversal but accepts `a/../../etc`.

recommendations.title: Close two narrow guard blind spots
recommendations.detail: Untracked-file digests truncate at 10 MiB, so edits past that point never invalidate diff-review — include the file size in the digest or hash the full stream. The session touch log is read-merge-write with no lock, so concurrent PreToolUse hooks can drop a repository — use a lock or O_EXCL append.

recommendations.title: Handle worktrees/jj workspaces in the local-exclude step and clean stray artifacts
recommendations.detail: project-bootstrap.sh only writes .git/info/exclude when .git is a directory, so in the builder's own workspace mode the settings file can leak into a commit — use `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`. Remove or relocate the tracked root plan.sidecar.json (its folio is missing) and the orphaned bin/anvil-guard.

recommendations.title: Bound the build skill's re-dispatch loop and scope review-fix-loop honestly
recommendations.detail: The build wave loop has no cap on re-dispatching a `blocked` builder (unlike review-fix-loop's converged/stalled/exhausted). review-fix-loop depends on Claude Code's /loop and suggests `git switch -c` while the builder is jj-only; mark it Claude-only or document a driver for the other harnesses.

recommendations.title: Tighten merge_research conflict detection
recommendations.detail: The merge flags a conflict whenever a topic has more than one distinct free-text `position`, so this packet reports 20 'conflicts' of which only two are real disagreements (hook install mechanism: README/bootstrap-tools symlink vs project-bootstrap copy; build-guard framing: advisory header vs blocking README). Either constrain positions to a small vocabulary per topic or require an explicit `contradicts` flag.
